analysis.title: Global Healthcare: Pharmaceuticals: Friday Fodder: Tailwinds Persisting
key_insights: Every large-cap biopharma company that has reported 3Q26 so far posted a topline beat, and many raised topline guidance. Most stocks rose on print day, with BIIB and GSK the exceptions. JNJ fell initially but has since recovered.

Inflows into the sector come from macro factors (defensive rotation on downside growth risk, rotation out of AI/Tech) and from micro factors (3Q earnings delivery versus more mixed MedTech results this week).
HC is the second best performing S&P 500 sector YTD, behind only Energy, with large-cap biopharma leading HC subsectors.

Pharma now trades at parity with the S&P 500 on forward P/E, versus a 7% discount a week ago and a 27% discount entering the year. GS cautions against over-relying on historical periods of premium valuation.
LLY's multiple has held constant YTD while estimate revisions drive upside. LLY posted solid 3Q results and a third consecutive guidance raise that comfortably beat expectations.

Earnings call themes: M&A appetite (BMY evaluating multiple opportunities, ABBV citing obesity, MRK citing immunology), cost control supporting profit beats (Roche, Novartis, Sanofi), vaccine hesitancy headwinds (GSK, MRK), 340B tailwinds (Novartis, Sanofi), and AI efforts being quantified (BMY).
ESMO conference: GS calls out AMGN, JNJ, MRK and MRNA for the most positive updates (practice-changing data) in large-cap coverage.

Next week brings the tail end of large-cap earnings (AMGN, MRNA, Novo Nordisk, PFE, VRTX) and the US midterm elections. Panelists from a GS Washington trip saw low near-term drug pricing risk, with more policy uncertainty in other parts of HC than in large-cap biopharma.
US biotech outperformed this week: XBI +5.53% and NBI +4.35% versus S&P 500 +1.19%, on rate tailwinds, rotation out of AI/tech, and positive earnings and clinical updates.

BIIB: top- and bottom-line beat. Drivers are subcutaneous Leqembi momentum, Syfovre commercial injection volume +18% y/y, and high-dose Spinraza driving switches. Phase 3 litifilimab data in SLE is due in 1H December, and GS estimates a +/-10-15% stock move if both studies succeed or fail. GS would buy post-data weakness.

INCY: commercial performance and raised FY26 guidance are encouraging. Key drivers into YE26+ are execution on pipeline programs (mCALR initial 1L myelofibrosis data at ASH, Dec 12-15) and business development.

ALNY: fundamentally in-line 3Q print, but guided to the lower end of the $4.2-4.5bn FY26 TTR revenue range (GSe $4.287bn). Visibility into 2027 is limited, with 340B headwinds. The stock trades near GS's ~$165/share value on flat Amvuttra revenue/OpEx and no pipeline value.
GILD: top- and bottom-line beat. Focus areas are anito-cel in 4L+ multiple myeloma (Dec 23 PDUFA), the Trodelvy collaboration with BNTX, and edecesertib (IRAK4) Phase 2a data in CLE at ACR on Nov 8.

REGN: solid commercial quarter with a topline beat, and Eylea HD demand appeared to drive performance. GS sees REGN as attractive on valuation, and is focused on pipeline levers and business development.

AMGN: Phase 3 DeLLphi-305 data for Imdelltra in 1L maintenance ES-SCLC received a standing ovation and was published in NEJM. GS believes it supports standard of care. Success in the DeLLphi-312 1L induction study would raise addressable US patients to ~23K from ~14K in 2L+.

MRNA/MRK: intismeran plus Keytruda in adjuvant melanoma showed RFS HR=0.58 (p<0.001), meeting the <0.60 bar, with HR=0.42 post 6 months. Early PDAC data showed 11/20 ongoing responses. RCC data is due late 2026/2027.

SMMT: partner Akeso's Phase 3 HARMONi-GI1 (China-only) in biliary tract cancer showed OS HR=0.75 (p=0.0031) for ivonescimab plus chemo versus Imfinzi plus chemo. Global Phase 3 HARMONi-3 in frontline NSCLC reads out by YE/early 2027, and investors expect a PFS HR of 0.72 or better.

EU Pharma: the SXDP is up c.14% in the past month on multiple expansion, with EU Pharma up c.9%. Guidance updates imply only c.1-2% earnings upgrade risk on average. Beats are helped by one-time items (revenue pull forward, gross-to-net benefits) and flat OpEx.

Bayer and Novo report next week. GS thinks consensus mis-models Bayer CropScience seasonality. For Novo, consensus anticipates strong Wegovy pill sales and a guidance upgrade, and Sanofi's read-across suggests 340B GTN adjustments could support Novo's insulin franchise, which consensus does not model.

Bayer is back at or above EUR 50 after positive Nubeqa prostate cancer data (could add EUR 1bn to GS peak sales) and a win in the Aretino case. If Judge Boyer approves the proposed settlement, GS believes shares could break above EUR 50.

Roche sales beat by 2%, helped by a Japan pull forward ahead of an ERP switchover (1% beat excluding it). Novartis sales were in line, but cost control drove an 8%/7% operating profit/EPS beat and a profitability guidance raise. Sanofi beat on sales and Business EPS by 26%, with new guidance implying c.5% upside risk to consensus. Dupixent US volumes are growing 17-18% against a EUR 25bn 2030 peak sales target that could look conservative.

Obesity scripts: overall GLP-1 obesity scripts rose 4% w/w, passing 1.4m weekly per IQVIA. Wegovy pill TRx rose c.6% to 183k, near the 184k high. Foundayo TRx rose c.9% to 63.1k, with TRx share at 26% (17% at the start of summer) and NBRx share at 37%. Orals hold c.34% NBRx share versus c.17% TRx share.

Pen TRx share is 33:67 Wegovy versus Zepbound, shifting toward Zepbound since July (42:58 before). Total market share is 36:64 in favour of Lilly, and NBRx share is 39:61 (43:57 capture adjusted). This supports LLY commentary that Medicare BRIDGE favours injectables.

AZN and GSK both beat on core EPS, but stocks diverged, driven by views on 2027. GSK faces a quiet catalyst path and HIV pipeline concerns. AZN was helped by the absence of cautious 2027 opex commentary. AZN's AVANZAR readout is delayed to 1Q27.

GMAB delivered positive petosemtamab data in head and neck cancer, completing all three of its 4Q catalysts, with the stock up over 100% in three months. ARGX's EMPASSION readout for empasiprubart is the key remaining high-profile readout into year end.
Generic Pharma is up 37% YTD (market-cap weighted), versus XLV +16% and the S&P 500 +13%. Next week TEVA and VTRS are expected in line, and AMRX has potential for a beat and raise.

Upcoming catalysts: ACR (Nov 6-11) with AMGN anti-CD40L Sjogren's data, CRSP and ALLO CAR-T data. ASH abstracts release Nov 4. Also BIIB SLE data in 1H December and ANNX Phase 3 geographic atrophy data, and an FDA decision on REGN's cemdisiran in gMG.

sector_views.rationale: Beat and raise earnings, continued inflows from defensive and AI/Tech rotation, and multiple expansion. Pharma is at parity with the S&P 500 on forward P/E.
Up 37% YTD. GS sees an attractive setup into YE26+ with healthy growth, launches and late-stage catalysts.

earnings_insights: Large-cap biopharma 3Q26: every company reported so far posted a topline beat (reported results, not estimates), and many raised topline guidance. Mean day-1 absolute performance was +236bps.
LLY reported 3Q26 on 10/29 with a topline beat and guidance raise. Post-earnings revisions: 2026 EPS +4.1%, 2027 EPS +4.1%.
BIIB reported 3Q26 on 10/28 with a top- and bottom-line beat. Stock fell 343bps on day 1.
GSK reported 3Q26 on 10/28 with a core EPS beat and reiterated guidance. Stock fell 432bps on day 1.
ALNY reported an in-line 3Q26 print and guided FY26 TTR revenue to the lower end of $4.2-4.5bn (GSe $4.287bn).
GILD reported 3Q26 after the close on 10/29 with a top- and bottom-line beat and a topline raise.
REGN reported 3Q26 on 10/30 with a topline beat.

Roche 3Q26 sales beat consensus by 2%, helped by a Japan pull forward (1% beat excluding it). Novartis 3Q26 sales were in line, with an 8% operating profit beat and 7% EPS beat, and profitability guidance was raised.
Sanofi 3Q26 beat on sales and Business EPS, with a 26% earnings beat. New guidance implies c.5% upside risk to consensus.
Novo Nordisk (reports next week): consensus anticipates strong Wegovy pill sales and a guidance upgrade, and 340B GTN adjustments in insulin are not currently modelled by consensus (GS view).
Bayer (reports next week): GS believes consensus mis-models CropScience seasonality.
TEVA and VTRS are expected to report in-line quarters next week, and AMRX has potential for a beat and raise. AMGN, MRNA, PFE and VRTX also report next week.
risk_factors: Vaccine hesitancy flagged by GSK and MRK as an ongoing headwind.
340B headwinds for ALNY and rising expectations and competitor data headline risk for Roche's giredestrant.
Long-term growth profile and post-2030 patent expirations for Novartis.
Bayer glyphosate litigation overhang, dependent on settlement approval.
Policy uncertainty in other parts of HC, and US midterm elections.
Historical analogs for Pharma premium valuation may not apply.
BIIB Phase 3 SLE data and HARMONi-3 results could move stocks sharply.
